title: Alice and Bob are playing heads and tails,
answer:
原题：Alice and Bob are playing heads and tails,

Alice tosses n + 1 coins, Bob tosses n coins. The coins are
fair. What is the probability that Alice will have strictly
more heads than Bob?

参考解答：Solution 1: Alice flips the coin more often than Bob, so
either she must end up with more heads or with more tails
than Bob. She cannot, however, end up with more heads
and more tails, because she only flips one more coin than
Bob. We deduce that either Alice gets more heads or she
gets more tails.

Since thie events are equally likely, they both have
probability + 3, and therefore the probanility that Alice will
have strictly more heads than Bob is 3.

Solution 2: Suppose that Alice and Bob begin by flipping
n coins each. Let p be the probability that Alice gets
more heads than Bob, and let q be the probability that
both Alice and Bob get an equal number of heads. Note
that 2p +q = 1 since the probability that Alice gets more



3.7. BRAINTEASERS 169

heads than Bob is, by symmetry, equal to the probability
that Bob gets more heads than Alice.

Alice then flips the (n + 1)st coin. For Alice to have
more heads, she either had more heads than Bob before
flipping the last coin; or the same number of heads as Bob
before flipping the last coin and her (n + 1)st flip must
come up heads. Hence, the probability of Alice winning
is p+ 3q.

Since 2p+q=1, thenp+$q=3. O

title: Alice is in a restaurant trying to decide
answer:
原题：Alice is in a restaurant trying to decide

between three desserts. How can she choose one of three
desserts with equal probability with the help of a fair coin?
What if the coin is biased and the bias is unknown?

参考解答：Solution 1: Denote the desserts by A, B, and C. First,
suppose the coin is fair. Denote heads by H and tails by
T. The procedure to choose one of three desserts with
equal probability is as follows: toss the coin twice; let
the outcomes TH, HT, and TT correspond to choosing
desserts A, B, and C, respectively; if the outcome is HH,
repeat the procedure.

Note that the probability of our procedure not being
repeated is p = 3; hence, the number of times our proce-
dure is repeated is a geometric random variable with p as
its parameter. The expected number of times our proce-
dure is repeated is = = :. Since each procedure involves
two coin tosses, the expected number of coin tosses before
Alice chooses one of three desserts with equal probability
is g.

Now, suppose the coin is biased. One procedure to
choose one of three desserts with equal probability would
be as follows: toss the coin four times; denote by TH HT,
HTTH, and THTH the outcomes corresponding to choos-
ing desserts A, B, and C, respectively; all the other 4-toss
outcomes result in repeating the procedure.


170 CHAPTER 3. SOLUTIONS

Solution 2: An alternative procedure is as follows: toss
the coin three times; denote by HTT, THT, and HTT
the outcomes corresponding to choosing desserts A, B,
and C, respectively; all the other 3-toss outcomes result
in repeating the procedure.

Using an argument similar to the case with a fair coin,
one finds that the expected number of tosses of a coin
with an unknown bias, before Alice chooses one of three
desserts with equal probability, is 84 and 8, respectively,
for the two procedures described above. OU

title: An ant is in the corner of a 10 x 10 x 10
answer:
原题：An ant is in the corner of a 10 x 10 x 10

room and wants to go to the opposite corner. What is the
length of the shortest path the ant can take?

参考解答：For clarity, assume that the ant is in a corner
by the ceiling. Denote that corner by A, and denote by
B the opposite corner to A, which is by the floor. The
shortest path from A to B would require the ant to go on
a straight line across a wall of the room to a side of the
floor and from there on a straight line along the floor to
the B. If you imagine laying down to the floor the vertical
wall the ant went down from A to the floor, you have a
10 x 20 rectangle with A and B opposite corners in the
rectangle. The shortest path for the ant to go from A to
B is by following the diagonal of the rectangle, which has
length 10/5 ~ 22.36. O

title: A 10 x 10 x 10 cube is made of 1, 000 unit
answer:
原题：A 10 x 10 x 10 cube is made of 1, 000 unit

cubes. How many unit cubes can you see on the outside?

参考解答：If all the outside unit cubes are removed, what
remains is an 8 x 8 x 8 cube, which is made of 8° = 512
unit cubes. Thus, there are 1000 — 512 = 488 outside unit
cubes. O

See page 27.

参考解答：The first part of this question asks us to compare

the value of call options struck on two different stocks which have the same

where py! # *. The answer is that despite their differing drifts, the prices of
the options on the two stocks do not differ at all. The more interesting question
is why they do not differ. Mathematically, we can consider the derivation of the
Black-Scholes equation in Question 2.1. Here we see that the pricing of any
derivative must be done in the risk-neutral measure in order to avoid arbitrage,
and under the risk-neutral measure the drift of a stock is changed so that

dSi = rSidt + oSidW,,

for i = 1,2, where r is the risk-free rate of return. Financially (from [6], Section
5.7), ‘this reflects the fact that the hedging strategy ensures that the underlying
drift of the stock is balanced against the drift of the option. The drifts are
balanced since drift reflects the risk premium demanded by investors to account
for uncertainty and that uncertainty has been hedged away’. That is we can
perfectly hedge the claim in the Black-Scholes world.

We now consider a call option on a stock with downward jumps at random
times compared to a model without jumps. In fact, we treat the more general
case of an option with a convex payoff (a call option is such an example). We
assume the usual Black-Scholes diffusion model for the stocks, with one having
an additional jump term.

To see how the prices compare, we carry out the Black-Scholes hedging
strategy. This consists of an initial portfolio cost of Cgg(0, So), where Ces
denotes the Black-Scholes (no-jumps) option price, and holding aCas units of
the stock while the rest is in bonds. While a jump does not occur, the hedge
works perfectly, and hence if no jumps occur the option’s payoff is perfectly
replicated.

The convex payoff of the call option leads to a convex Black-Scholes price.
This implies that if we graph the price as a function of spot for any time ¢, any
tangent of the graph will lie below it. The above Black-Scholes hedge we set
up is constructed to be exactly the tangent through the point (5;, Cgs(t, S:)).


2.3. SOLUTIONS 29

When a jump occurs, we will move instantly along this tangent line, and hence
finish at a point which is below the Black-Scholes price. We continue to hedge
as before, and further jumps will add to this difference in the hedging portfolio
and the Black-Scholes price. Hence if a jump occurs the portfolio value will be
less than the Black-Scholes price.

Overall, we constructed a portfolio with initial cost Cgs(0, 59) which some-
times finishes with the same value as the option (if no jumps occur) and sometimes
finishes with a lower value (if a jump occurs). Thus by no arbitrage considerations
the value of the option on the stock with jumps must be greater than Cgg(0, So).

For further information on pricing using a model with jumps, see [6] Ch.15.

参考解答：The key to this question is relating the American

optionality of option A to the European optionality of option B in terms of

If we were to assume that the stock follows Geometric Brownian motion it
will have a negative drift in the case of zero interest rates (due to the —0?T/2
term). We no longer have that option B is worth half the value of option A, it
will be worth less than half the value of A.

title: What uses could an option be put to?
answer:
原题：What uses could an option be put to?

参考解答：The short answer to any question about participa-

tion in the financial markets is that there are three sorts of behaviours:

e hedging,
e speculation,
e arbitrage.

A hedger uses financial products to reduce risk. For example, an exporter
who is paid in foreign currency may use an option to guard against the possibility
that the exchange rate moves against him.

A speculator takes on risk with the belief either that the compensation for
the additional risk makes it worthwhile or because he has specific views on how
an asset will behave, and the product allows him to make a profit from these
views if they are correct.

An arbitrageur exploits mis-pricing in the market, and makes money by
buying risk in one place and selling it in another.

title: Suppose spot today is 90. A call option is struck at 100
answer:
原题：Suppose spot today is 90. A call option is struck at 100

and expires in one year. There are no interest rates. Spot moves log-normally
in a perfect Black-Scholes world. I claim that I can hedge the option for free.
Whenever spot crosses 100 in an upwards direction I borrow 100 and buy the
stock. Whenever spot crosses 100 in a downwards direction I sell the stock and
repay my loan. At expiry either the option is out-of-the-money in which case I
have no position or it is in-the-money and I use the 100 dollar strike to payoff
my loan. Thus the option has been hedged for free. Where is the error in this
argument?

参考解答：This is a tricky one in that you often find that the

questioner does not really understand the problem either.

The fundamental problem is that the hedging strategy is not well defined.
For example, when you first touch 100, how do you know whether the stock will
go up or down? It is not clear at that time whether 100 will be crossed so you
cannot know what to hold. Thus you really need to buy at 100+ « and sell at
100 —. You then lose 2¢ for each crossing, and the strategy is no longer riskless.

The properties of Brownian motion actually make the problem worse. If it
hits a level then it will hit it again infinitely often in an arbitrarily small amount
of time. So even in retrospect, it’s hard to know when the crossing occurred.

title: Assume you have a good trading model that you think will
answer:
原题：Assume you have a good trading model that you think will

make money. What information would you present to your manager to support
your claim.

2.2.6. Trees and Monte Carlo.

参考解答：We will answer this question assuming two

different models. Firstly we consider a statistical arbitrage model and then
secondly assuming we have a model for pricing exotic derivatives.

Statistical arbitrage involves exploiting small mispricings in the market,
usually by buying and selling stocks to create a portfolio which has minimal
risk, but potential for profit. This portfolio of stocks will often be very large, and
thus requiring a large amount of computational power. Therefore one aspect of a
good model is that it returns trade information in a useful time frame.

What other information would you use to prove your model is a good one? A
good check is to back-test the model, seeing how the trades it suggested actually
worked on historic data. One could then argue if it made money in the past it
should make money in the future. An important test is that it should work “out
of sample” that is if we train on a set of data then it should work on real data
that it has not been trained on.

Typically, statistical arbitrage (also known as “stat arb” or “stab art’) works
well in normal times but fails when turbulence occurs. You therefore might want
to demonstrate that it still works in a period of turbulence. If you could prove
that your model not only makes money in benign markets, but it also does well
during a market crash, then your manager will no doubt be interested to hear
more.

Another point to consider is whether the trading strategy takes into account
bid-offer spreads and other transaction costs. It is easy to find strategies that


64 2. OPTION PRICING

work when these are ignored, and this will be one of the first things your boss
seizes upon.

A related issue is liquidity. Many funds and most spectacularly, LTCM, have
failed because of a sudden liquidity drought. How much money will your strategy
lose in such a case?

Now considering exotic derivatives; the first piece of evidence to present
would be that your model reproduces the prices of basic instruments. If the
model cannot accurately price vanilla options and discount bonds, then traders
will need a lot of convincing that it will price exotic instruments correctly.

The second piece of evidence to present comes down to what a model should
actually do. Apart from giving prices, a model’s main purpose is to suggest a
hedging strategy. Therefore a new model that provides more accurate hedging
ratios, will be popular automatically. How could you provide proof that the
hedging is more accurate? Once again we could run back-testing on market data.
If the variance of the profit and loss to a trading book is less under your new
model than the current model, the hedging is more accurate and hence you have
a better model.

In addition, you will have to discuss the advantages of the model over the
old. These could include

e speed;

e realism;

e ease of calibration;

e ability to easily specify new products.

title: Follow-up: given that we have seen that trinomial trees do
answer:
原题：Follow-up: given that we have seen that trinomial trees do

not lead to unique prices, why do banks use them to compute prices?

参考解答：The crucial point here is that when using a model

as a computational device, we are not doing no arbitrage arguments. Instead,
we are approximating a given risk-neutral measure. In this case, the risk-neutral
measure we are approximating is geometric Brownian motion with a growth rate
of r.


68 2. OPTION PRICING

We can think of four operations:

Passing to the risk-neutral measure.
Discretization with a trinomial tree.
Pricing.

Passing to the limit.

The crucial point here is that the first two of these do not commute.

One reason why a trinomial tree is a useful computational device is that it
does not naturally oscillate in the same was as a binomial tree. That is if the
number of time steps in the tree changes by one, the price will not change as
much as in a binomial tree. Trinomial trees also have much flexibility in terms of
node placement since one can play with 3 node locations and two probabilities,
whereas with a binomial tree there are two node locations and one probability.
We have to match two quantities (at least asymptotically): mean and variance.
This means that one can adapt node placement to the product, so, for example,
nodes lie on barriers.

title: Explain the Longstaff-Schwartz algorithm for pricing an
answer:
原题：Explain the Longstaff-Schwartz algorithm for pricing an

early exercisable option with Monte Carlo.


22 2. OPTION PRICING
2.2.7. Incomplete markets.

参考解答：As we saw in Question 2.55 it is difficult to use

Monte Carlo for products with early exercise features, such as American options.
The Longstaff—Schwartz method is one way to handle early exercise using Monte
Carlo.

When pricing an early exercisable product, we need to know at a given time
whether it will be worth more by exercising now or by holding onto it. The
value of holding onto the option, known as the continuation value, is what the
Longstaff-Schwartz method estimates via regression. The Longstaff—Schwartz
method is commonly used for such products as Bermudan swaptions.


2.3, SOLUTIONS 71

Before we jump into the algorithm, a few details are necessary. A regression
needs to be carried out against some basis functions, for example we might
regress y against some explanatory variables x and x. Choosing good basis
functions that will estimate the continuation value accurately is very much an
art.

The Longstaff—Schwartz algorithm is:

(1) Run a certain number of Monte Carlo paths (e.g. 1000) and store the
exercise value divided by the numeraire at each possible exercise date
for each path. We also need to store the value of the basis functions at
the same points.

(2) With all this data we now look at the second last exercise date. We
perform a regression (usually least-squares) of the value at the last
exercise date against the basis functions. This gives coefficients, a;, for
the basis functions.

(3) Using these coefficients we can calculate the continuation value at
the second last exercise time for each path, using for example y =
aye+ aor”.

(4) We now replace the deflated exercise value stored initially with the
continuation value, if the continuation value is greater.

(5) Continue back through the exercise dates until reaching time 0. The
(biased) value of the product will be the average of the time zero values
multiplied by the initial numeraire value.

title: Explain why a stochastic volatility model gives a smile.
answer:
原题：Explain why a stochastic volatility model gives a smile.


2.3. Solutions

2.3.1. Black-Scholes.

参考解答：A stochastic volatility model takes volatility to be

driven by a random process. It is then possible that the volatility will become
large causing large movements in the underlying asset price. These large moves
give the distribution of the underlying asset fatter tails than in the Black-Scholes
model. This means that options away from the money will be priced more
expensively than in Black-Scholes leading to a volatility smile.

Another way to think about why the smile occurs is by looking at the
second derivative of the option price with respect to the volatility. In the Black—
Scholes world our Vega sensitivity (how good our volatility hedge is) will be
zero. However, a stochastic volatility model will not necessarily have a non-zero
derivative of Vega, therefore there is Vega convexity which is related to the
volatility smile.

CHAPTER 3

Probability

3.1. Introduction

This chapter focuses on questions from probability and stochastic processes.
There is an inevitable overlap with Chapter 2, since random processes are at the
core of modern pricing theory.

Problems range from the elementary, e.g., “what is the expectation of a single
roll of a fair die?’, to the rather hard. The interviewer is looking for two things:
the ability to think probabilistically, and evidence of having studied stochastic
processes. We have divided the questions between general problems many of
which involve coin tosses, and questions about stochastic processes.

For the more challenging questions, we include references to allow the
reader to study all the details. Before attempting quant job interviews, a study of
probability theory is a must; here are several excellent books on the topic:

“Elementary Probability Theory” by Kai Lai Chung is a great place to start.
The text is primarily aimed at people doing a first undergraduate course in
probability. The book also includes a chapter on financial mathematics.

“Probability and Random Processes” by Geoffrey Grimmett and David
Stirzaker is slightly more challenging than Chung. The book is well presented
and worth reading.

Another excellent book covering basic probability (and continuing to more
advanced topics) is William Feller’s two volume “An Introduction to Probability
Theory and its Applications’. Volume I covers discrete distributions and events,
Volume II moves onto the continuous treatment. The explanations are presented
in a clear and concise manner.

719


80 3. PROBABILITY

If you have some probability knowledge, “Probability with Martingales” by
David Williams is a great place to start for discrete time martingales. The style
is clear and informative while presenting solid mathematical ideas.

Following on from this, try the two volume set “Diffusions, Markov Processes
and Martingales” by Chris Rogers and David Williams. Much of the material
from Williams is repeated quickly in this book, before they proceed to discuss
the basics of Brownian motion and continuous time martingales. The second
volume discusses stochastic calculus.

“Introduction to Stochastic Integration” by Kai Lai Chung and Ruth Williams
is a very readable account of stochastic integration theory. It assumes knowledge
of continuous time martingales, however, so you must learn that elsewhere first.

If you want books with a more mathematical finance approach, “The Concepts
and Practice of Mathematical Finance” by the first author of this book, Mark
Joshi, is an excellent place to start.

answer:

参考解答：There are many ways to do this. One particularly

We gamble in such a way that we make money on heads but such that if we

easy. The probability that coins 3k, 3k + 1,3k + 2 are all heads is 1/8. So the
probability that we have not obtained three heads in a row after 3k draws is less
than

CHAPTER 4

Interest rates

4.1. Introduction

The area of interest rates, specifically interest rate options, usually requires
the most complicated quant work. The main reason for this is that an interest
rate derivative depends on the yield curve, which is a one-dimensional object, as
opposed to an equity or FX option which depends on a zero-dimensional object:
the stock price or FX rate.

Since these options are fairly complex, for entry-level jobs detailed knowledge
of interest rate pricing is rarely expected. However, if the job you are applying
for is on an interest rate options desk, you would be expected to demonstrate
some real interest and understanding of the topic.

It is therefore worth taking the time to understand the most common interest
rates (e.g. forward and swap rates) and also the most commonly used model, the
LIBOR market model (LMM or BGM).

The LIBOR market model is not too difficult to understand, but there are
many subtleties regarding implementation. One of the best ways to understand
the model is therefore to implement it yourself. A good place to start is by trying
Computer Project 11 in [6].

Some introductory books containing chapters on interest rates models are

e “The Concepts and Practice of Mathematical Finance” by Mark Joshi,
[6]. This contains a chapter on forward rate agreements and swaps and
a chapter on the LMM but does not discuss short rate models.

e “Financial Calculus,” by M. Baxter and A. Rennie, [1]. This contains
an overview of the main short rate models.

title: What is the difference between an inline function and a macro
answer:
原题：What is the difference between an inline function and a macro

in C++?

参考解答：This question is a little strange in that there is

an implication that the two are similar, whereas they actually have very little
in common.

We first discuss the keyword inline. Placing this in front of a function
declaration tells the compiler that you would like it to replace each call to the
function with the code inside the function. This then eliminates the overhead of
making a call to the function.

There are subtleties, however:

it is a suggestion to the compiler not a command to the compiler;

e the code may be longer because the definition of the function is repeated
many times;

e the code must be included in the header file so as to be available to
clients, so changing it will cause a lot to recompile, and any compile-
time dependencies it has, will also be dependencies for clients;

e and on the plus side, the fact that the code is available to the compiler
in context of use may allow the compiler to use extra optimizations;

e adding or removing inline should never affect anything other than the
efficiency of your program.


236 7. CODING IN C++

A macro is not actually anything to do with the compiler. Instead, it is an
instruction to C-preprocessor or Cpp. The Cpp reorganizes a file before the
compiler starts work by including all files specified, and by expanding macros.
A macro is therefore a direct text to text substitution which takes places before
the compiler does its job. As such it is a much more error prone tool and should
generally be avoided.

The main thing the two approaches have in common is that they allow the
coding of simple functions in such a way that they can be used without the
run-time overhead of a function call, and without duplicating code.

title: It is permissible to throw in a constructor in C++? Justify
answer:
原题：It is permissible to throw in a constructor in C++? Justify

your answer.

参考解答：This is a tricky one in that the community seems

to be split between those who think it is wrong to throw in a constructor, and
those who think it is silly not to. The best response is therefore to say that you
know that there are varying opinions on this, and list the pros and cons, and
then finish up with your opinion.

The crucial fact to know is that if you throw in a constructor then the
destructor for the object is not called. And it will never be called since the object
will not exist after a throw during its construction. However, the destructor for
each fully-constructed data member is called. If you are in the main part of the
constructor that is within the curly brackets, then all the data members are fully
constructed and therefore destroyed.

The main argument against throwing in a constructor is that the destructor
will not be called, and therefore it will not do the clean-up that is usually
done when the object is destroyed. For example, any memory allocated in the
constructor will not be released.

It is therefore OK to throw in a constructor provided you ensure that every-
thing is properly destroyed and deallocated. The easiest way to do this is to use


7.3. SOLUTIONS 237

smart pointers as data members instead of raw pointers. These will be destroyed
on exit and will automatically carry out the required deallocations.

If you make the rule of no throws in constructor, the problem is what do you
do if some aspect of construction fails? Constructors do not have return values
so you cannot return a failure code. You could create an extra method for every
class that says whether construction was successful. Every time you construct
an object, a test for success would then be required together with necessary
remedial action. This would be rather painful.

title: Is it permissible to throw in a destructor in C++? Justify your
answer:
原题：Is it permissible to throw in a destructor in C++? Justify your

answer.

参考解答：This is less controversial than the analagous question

for a constructor, though you do get the odd contrarian. There are good reasons
to never do this.

The fundamental problem is that if two unhandled exceptions exist simul-
taneously then the C++ standard says that the application will terminate. If
destructors are allowed to throw then it is very hard to avoid two happening at
once: when an exception is thrown all automatic (i.e. ordinary) objects declared
in the current scope are destroyed before the catch is executed. If any of their
destructors can throw, you get two at once and a crash.

So never ever throw in a destructor.

title: How would you copy a polymorphic object of unknown type?
answer:
原题：How would you copy a polymorphic object of unknown type?

参考解答：This is a standard problem and it is discussed at

great length in [7]. The standard way to do this is by using a virtual constructor.
Note that it is not possible to declare a standard constructor virtual but we can
achieve the same effects by making a class method virtual.

We therefore define in the base class

virtual Base* clone() const =0;

and in each inherited class

virtual Inherited* clone() const
{
return new Inherited(*this) ;

}

The crucial point here is that the inherited class knows its own type and so can
copy itself without any problems. The return type is a pointer to an object of
the class allocated on the heap since the type is unknown to the calling code.

Note also that the return type is a pointer to the inherited class not the base
class; this changing of return types is allowed when overriding in an inherited
class.

title: What is a virtual destructor and when is it needed?
answer:
原题：What is a virtual destructor and when is it needed?

参考解答：If one has an object of some inherited class that

has been dynamically allocated (i.e. created using new, ) then when it is deleted
via a pointer to a base class object, one has the issue that the correct destructor
needs to be called. If the destructor of the base class is virtual, then the inherited
class one is called directly and there is no problem.

If it is not virtual, then the base class destructor is called and the object may
not be properly deleted. This generally causes a memory leak and may cause
worse problems.

As a general rule, always declare destructors virtual if any method is pure
abstract, i.e. not defined in the base class. Some compilers, e.g. g++, generate
a warning if you do not declare the destructor virtual in this case. Generally
declare them virtual if any method is virtual. If no method is virtual it probably
is not necessary.

title: If a class B is derived from class A and contains an object
answer:
原题：If a class B is derived from class A and contains an object

of class C, in which order are the constructors/destructors called for an object
of type B.

参考解答：The basic rule is the more fundamental something

is, the sooner it is constructed and the later it is destructed. The reason for this is
that an inherited class may want to use the base class during either construction
or destruction, but the converse will never be true. NB if you attempt to use the
inherited class via a virtual function during base class construction you will come
to grief. If the function is pure virtual you will get a run-time error saying you
called a pure virtual function. If it is not, the base class version will be called.

So in this particular case, A is constructed then C then B. And for destruction,
B then C then A. Note that this means the class data members are available in
the constructor and destructor of B.

title: What does every class come equipped with?
answer:
原题：What does every class come equipped with?

参考解答：The compiler will always provide a copy con-

structor, an assignment operator and a destructor. It is important to realize that
these are trivial in the sense that they do the simplest thing they can.

The copy constructor therefore calls the copy constructor of each data member
to make a copy. This is called making a shallow copy. The assignment operator
calls the assignment operator of each data member.

It is OK to use the shallow copy if every data member has a copy constructor
that does the right thing. This is generally not the case if data members are
pointers, since both old and new objects will point to the same data. This can
result in crashes when the pointed-to object is deleted twice. The same issues
apply with assignment operators.

A non-trivial destructor is needed if and only if the class needs to free
resources when the object dies. This is typically deleting allocated memory. A
trivial destructor should be declared virtual if the object is likely to be deleted
via a pointer to a base class.

The best way to get round declaring non-trivial copy constructors, destructors
and assignment operators is to use smart pointers that do all the correct things
when the default behaviour is used. This has been dubbed (by Mark Joshi) “the
rule of almost zero.”

operator B() const;

in the class declaration for A. When we define the operator, we code it as

B::operator A() const
{
// create object of type B and return it

title: Why does a class that uses memory allocation need a
answer:
原题：Why does a class that uses memory allocation need a

properly written copy constructor and assignment operator?

参考解答：If a class uses memory allocation then it will use

the new command. This returns a pointer to a piece of dynamically allocated mem-
ory. If we make the pointer a class data member, then the operations of copying
and assignment will cause issues if we use the compiler’s default operators.

29

In particular, the copy constructor supplied by the compiler will be a “shallow
copy constructor, that is it will simply make a copy of the pointer. The effect
of this is that the original object and the copy will point to the same piece
of allocated memory. This will cause many problems. For example, a properly
written object should delete the pointed-to memory in its destructor if not
before. A shallow copy will cause this to happen twice, and a crash will result.

More generally, even if the deletion is handled correctly in some other way,
the two objects will be strongly tied together and the behaviour will not be that
of a copying an ordinary object. The issues with assignment are similar, plus
there is an additional complication that the object being overwritten will lose its
pointer to the memory it had previously allocated. This means that that memory
will never be deallocated and a memory leak occurs.

Some additional points to note on this problem are that the class will also
need a properly written destructor and that many of the problems can be avoided
by using smart pointers. It is also worth mentioning at this point “the rule
of three”: if a class has one of a destructor, copy constructor and assignment
operator, it generally needs all three.

Personally, I prefer the “rule of almost zero”: a class should have none of
the three except an empty virtual destructor when it has abstract methods. The
reason for this is that memory allocation and deallocation is much better handled


7.3. SOLUTIONS 247

by smart pointers. Write (or find in Boost) once a smart pointer class that has
the desired behaviours, and then use and reuse that. This is a lot less bug prone
and takes a lot less time when writing new classes. For more on the rule of
almost zero see the second edition of [7].

title: Write the code for a sorting algorithm. Discuss the speed
answer:
原题：Write the code for a sorting algorithm. Discuss the speed

and memory of your program. How can you improve it?


7.2. QUESTIONS 227

参考解答：The optimal solution to sort an array is to use

the Standard Library:

#include

MyArray // uses STL sort algorithm to sort input
STLSort (const MyArray& input // array to sort

)
{
MyArray tmp(input) ;
std: :sort(tmp.begin(), tmp.end());
return tmp;
}

This will not do it in place. If you want to do it without copying the array, then
don’t copy the array, change the input to non-const and the return type to void.

It is unlikely that the interviewer will be satisfied with this response, however,
since they are probably trying to test your skill with algorithms. It is also worth
knowing that the STL sort algorithm is not guaranteed to be a stable sort, that
is it can change the order of equivalent elements (i.e. neither a < b not b > a.)
If they ask you for a stable algorithm use stable_sort instead.


248 7. CODING IN C++

Here is a simple implementation of the insert sort algorithm:

template
void InsertSort(T start, T end)

{
for(T i=start; i {
T::value_type value = *i;
T dec = i;
while(dec > start && *(dec-1)>=value)
{
*dec=*(dec-1);
--dec;
}
*dec=value;
}
}

The type T is an iterator (or pointer). This allows the code to be generic and
applied to a vector of any type with comparison operators. Insert sort is simple
but not particularly fast. It works as follows:

e Sort first 7 elements.

e Take element 7 + 1 and sift upwards until you find the place where it
fits in.

e Insert element j + 1 in the correct position and shuffle the elements
downwards to get the first 7 + 1 elements to be sorted.

e Keep on going until 7 reaches the end.

Important points to know about it are:

e It is stable.
e It is in-place and requires no extra memory.


7.3. SOLUTIONS 249

e It is order n in complexity.

e The speed depends on how sorted the array already is. If the array is
sorted then the speed is order n.

e It can be used incrementally. i.e. sort a stream of numbers as they arrive
rather than having to see them all before starting.

There exist faster algorithms which are order n log n. One easy such algorithm
is merge sort. With merge sort, one sorts the top half and bottom, and then
merges the two. To sort each half, we can recursively call merge until the array
is of length one. The main downside of this algorithm is that it is really fiddly to
implement without extra temporary memory. Note that one could shift to using
another algorithm once the array got small, e.g. use insert sort if length is less
than 20.

Other algorithms that are popular are heap sort and quick sort. There is
extensive discussion on Wikipedia of the pros and cons of various choices.

7.3. SOLUTIONS 251

class. Each object from a class with virtual functions will contain a pointer to

title: What is the problem with virtualization from the point of
answer:
原题：What is the problem with virtualization from the point of

view of optimization? What can a compiler do when a function is not virtualized?

参考解答：There are a number of issues with virtual functions

and optimization. The first is that they are typically called using pointer indirection,
that is the processor has to jump to a location contained in a pointer rather than
a pre-determined location. This results in a few extra instructions.

The second is more serious: if the compiler and linker do not know what is
contained in the function call they cannot perform any optimizations based on
its contents. In particular, virtual functions cannot be inlined.

In addition, a virtual function table will be created for the class and every
object from the class will need to contain a pointer to it. For large numbers of
small objects, this can be a real issue.


252 7. CODING IN C++

One should realize that these are not huge issues unless the code contained
in the function is very short. Thus it makes sense when a method is complicated
for it to be virtual but for accessor functions there can be a real performance hit.

title: Give all the places where you could use the keyword static.
answer:
原题：Give all the places where you could use the keyword static.

参考解答：The keyword static has many uses in C++. The

first and most common one is a static variable in a function.

Such a variable is initialized the first time it is encountered, but does not
go out of scope when the function exits, instead the value persists until the
next time the function is called and it is then reused. This had the advantage of
mimicking class-like behaviour in C but is less useful in C++. It can be used
in C++ to reduce the time spent on creating objects. Note, however, that this
use is incompatible with multi-threaded programming since the function could
be entered by two different threads both wanting to access the same data. It is
used in the singleton pattern to allow one instance of a class to exist which is a
static variable member inside a static member function.


272 7. CODING IN C++

This brings us on to static member functions, such a function is a method
of a class which is not associated with an object of the class. It is therefore
invoked via

MyClass: :MyMethod() ;

rather than

MyObject .MyMethod() ;

The third use of static is to specify a function which has no linkage outside
the translation unit. In other words, if we declare a function static, we cannot
call it from another file. This usage is archaic, since it has been replaced by the
concept of an anonymous namespace. It is has now been officially deprecated.

The fourth use of static is to denote class data members for which there
is only one copy for the entire class rather than one for each object in the class.
Once again there are issues with thread safety.

title: Define the following terms

e What is polymorphism?

参考解答：Polymorphism means “many shapes.” It used in

C++ to describe the process of having a base class with virtual functions that
are defined in inherited classes. Thus client code treats an object as if it is a
base class object but elements of its behaviour will vary according to which
inherited class it is from.

A good example of this is a Payoff class for which the main pay-off is only
defined in an inherited class. Thus either a call or a put pay-off could be passed


7.3. SOLUTIONS 273

into a routine that treats all pay-offs the same. For further discussion of this
example, see [7]. Other standard examples are “a car is a vehicle” with a “drive’
method and “a circle is a shape” with a “draw” method.

>

An abstract class is a class than contains a pure virtual method. A method
is pure virtual if it is virtual and has the specifier =O at the end. A class is also
pure virtual if it is inherited from a pure virtual class and does not override
the pure virtual with a non-pure one. An abstract class cannot be instantiated.
This means that such a class can only be used via an inherited class which is
concrete that is not pure virtual. Note that a pure virtual method need not be
defined anywhere but it can be if so desired.

A pointer is a variable that contains the address of another object. A reference
is also such a variable. The principal difference is that a reference can only
refer to one object which is determined when the reference is created, whereas a
pointer can be reassigned to refer to another object. Pointers can also point to
nothing and are then called NULL pointers and have the value zero.

CHAPTER 8

Logic/Brainteasers

8.1. Introduction

This chapter covers a range of cunning, tricky and devious questions. There is
little (if any) mathematics involved in solving the questions, instead they usually
require you to look at the question from the correct perspective. The keys to
success are therefore persistence and practice: there are only so many different
sorts of brainteasers and classifying the questions helps a lot.

Most of these problems are easily solved once you know the trick, so it is
particularly important you attempt them before checking the solution.

Due to the varied nature of the problems, there is no one ‘rule’ we can
suggest for tackling them. Here are some general pointers, however:

(1) Avoid the junk. A lot of these types of questions are presented in a
story-telling kind of way. Look through all the fluff that surrounds the
important details and focus on the main problem.

(2) Reduce the problem to a simple case and see what happens. If you’re
asked how to solve the problem for a group of objects, what happens
with one object? Two? Three? Can you see a pattern developing?

(3) Work backwards. If you’re asked to solve the problem over a number
of steps, how would you proceed if you were close to your goal? And
a little further...?

(4) Perhaps most importantly, think carefully! A lot of these problems are
written to trick you, so it is worth taking the extra thirty seconds to
consider them carefully.

answer:

参考解答：This is a test of basic deductive logic. We are

testing the truth of a statement of the form “P implies Q.” This means that if P
holds then Q must also hold. This is logically equivalent to “not Q implies not
P” so Q not holding means that P does not hold either.

It does not say anything about what is on the back of odd-numbered cards.
The question is ambiguous in that it is not clear whether a card must have a
letter on one side and a number on the other. We proceed as if this were the
case.

The first card “7” is odd so we should check the back. If the back has a
vowel, then the claim is false.

The second card “6” is even so the statement does not say anything about
this card. The other side may have a vowel, or it may not.

The third card “A” is a vowel, so we must check that the back is even.

The fourth card “C” is not a vowel, so the statement says nothing and we
not look at the back.

title: Suppose there are nine marbles in a jar, one heavier than the
answer:
原题：Suppose there are nine marbles in a jar, one heavier than the

rest. You have a set of scales and can weigh as many as you want a maximum of
three times to ascertain which marble is the heaviest. How do you achieve this?

参考解答：On each weighing, we can split the marbles in

half and eliminate one half as not containing the heaviest. This would indicate
that with one weighing we could compare two marbles, with two weighings four
marbles and with three weighings eight marbles. So how do we find the heaviest
from a group of nine?

The above reasoning only uses two possible outcomes: if all marbles are
weighed then either the first group is heavier or the second group is heavier.
However, if we leave some marbles out we introduce a third possibility: that the
third group is the one containing the heavier marble. This will be obvious if the
two groups weighed have an equal weight.

With this in mind, how do we solve our problem? On our first weighing,
compare two groups of four marbles, leaving the ninth marble out. If the two
groups of four are of equal weight, the ninth must be the heaviest and we are
done. If one of the groups is heavier, we are in the situation of having two
weighings remaining with four marbles. The problem is easily solved by weighing
two groups of two to find the heaviest pair, and then using your last weighing to
find which of the pair is the heaviest.

title: There are n lions in a cage. A piece of meat is thrown
answer:

It is unwise to argue with the interviewer over how silly this problem is. (It is,
of course, very silly!)

This sort of problem should always be done by induction. You start with no

If no lions, nothing happens.
If one lion, he eats the meat.

If two lions, no one eats the meat since if they do we will be back to one
lion, and the lion who ate the meat will be eaten by the above rule.

If three lions, the closest lion eats the meat since they know two lions will
not eat the meat.

If four lions, don’t eat.
If five lions, do eat.

In conclusion, if the number of lions is even no one eats. If the number of
lions is odd, one eats it.

days per year he can tune 800 pianos. There is therefore approximately 60 piano
tuners in Oxford.

The numbers used in this example are very approximate (and probably wrong)
and aren’t as important as the way in which the problem is broken down.

CHAPTER 9

The soft interview

9.1. Introduction

The good news is that quant teams tend to interview technically and Human
Resources are an afterthought. If this does not sound like good news to you,
then you would do well to reconsider your career choice. The bad news is that
“soft” questions are sometimes asked, and for fresh graduate jobs this sort of
thing can be important.

In this chapter, we therefore go through some of the questions that might
be asked and discuss how to handle them. Having prepared answers for all of
these will greatly help if the soft interview occurs. We then follow up with some
general finance questions that test your general awareness of finance.

title: 五个海盗分金币
answer:
海盗按资历从高到低编号5→1。最年长的海盗提出分配方案，所有海盗投票，≥50%同意则通过，否则扔下船由下一个提议。

关键思路：从小规模开始递推
• 2人：P2拿全部，P1得0
• 3人：P3给P1一枚（P1知道如果P3死自己得0），P3拿99枚
• 4人：P4给P2一枚，P4拿99枚
• 5人：P5给P1和P3各一枚，自己拿98枚

最终答案：P5拿98枚，P1和P3各拿1枚，P2和P4拿0枚。
💡 核心技巧：问题简化法 —— 先从最简单的2人情况开始，逐步增加复杂度，找到规律后推广。

title: 老虎与羊
answer:
100只老虎和1只羊在岛上。老虎可以吃羊，但吃后自己变成羊。所有老虎都聪明且理性，想存活。

递推分析：
• n=1：老虎会吃羊（无后顾之忧）
• n=2：不吃（吃了变羊，会被另一只老虎吃）
• n=3：吃（变羊后，剩下2只老虎不会吃）
• n=4：不吃（变羊后，剩下3只会吃）

规律：偶数只老虎 → 羊不被吃；奇数只老虎 → 羊被吃。
100是偶数，所以羊不会被吃。

title: 四人过桥
answer:
A(10分钟)、B(5分钟)、C(2分钟)、D(1分钟)需过桥，桥最多2人，黑夜需手电筒，按慢者速度走。

最优方案（17分钟）：
1. C和D先过桥 → 2分钟
2. D拿手电筒回来 → 1分钟
3. A和B过桥 → 10分钟
4. C拿手电筒回来 → 2分钟
5. C和D再次过桥 → 2分钟

💡 关键：让最慢的A和B一起过桥，且不让他们中任何一人走回头路。

title: 生日问题（逻辑推理版）
answer:
10个可能日期：3月4/5/8日、6月4/7日、9月1/5日、12月1/2/8日。
A知道月份，C知道日期。
A："我不知道生日，C也不知道。" → 月份不是6月或12月（因为6月7日和12月2日的日期唯一）
C："我原来不知道，现在知道了。" → 在3月和9月中，日期必须唯一 → 不是3月5日或9月5日
A："现在我也知道了。" → 如果是3月仍有两种可能(3月4/8)，所以必须是9月

答案：9月1日

title: 纸牌游戏（对称性应用）
answer:
每次翻两张牌：两张黑→庄家，两张红→你，一红一黑→丢弃。你比庄家牌多则赢$100。

答案：不应付钱玩这个游戏。

每次丢弃的牌对中有一红一黑，所以丢弃的红牌和黑牌数量相等。剩余的红牌（你的牌）和黑牌（庄家的牌）数量始终相等。你永远不可能赢。
💡 核心技巧：对称性分析 —— 丢弃的每对牌都包含一红一黑，因此你与庄家的牌堆永远等大。

title: 烧绳子计时45分钟
answer:
两根绳子各需1小时烧完，但密度不均匀。

方案：
1. 同时点燃第一根绳的两端 + 第二根绳的一端
2. 30分钟后第一根绳烧完，第二根还剩30分钟的量
3. 此时点燃第二根绳的另一端
4. 第二根绳再过15分钟烧完

总计：30 + 15 = 45分钟

title: 12球称量问题
answer:
12个相同球中有一个偏重或偏轻，用天平3次称量找出。

关键：分3组而非2组
将12球分为3组(1-4)、(5-8)、(9-12)

第1次：称(1-4) vs (5-8)
• 若平衡：坏球在9-12中，用已知正常球辅助，2次可定位
• 若不平衡：坏球在偏重或偏轻的那组中，通过交换称量缩小范围

通过构建决策树，3次称量可覆盖所有 24 种可能性（偏重12种 + 偏轻12种）。
💡 一般规律：n次称量可从 3ⁿ 个球中找出坏球（已知偏重/轻方向）；若不知道方向，可从 (3ⁿ-3)/2 个球中找出。

title: 100!末尾有多少个零
answer:
末尾零的数量取决于因子对(2×5)的数量。2的数量远多于5，所以数5的因子个数。

• 1-100中5的倍数：100/5 = 20个
• 其中25的倍数（额外贡献一个5）：100/25 = 4个

末尾零 = 20 + 4 = 24个

title: 25匹马赛马问题
answer:
25匹马，5条赛道，找前3名最快马。

需要7场比赛：
1. 分5组各跑1场（共5场），记录组内排名
2. 5个组的第1名跑第6场，确定全场第1
3. 第6场的第2、3名所在组可能有马进入前3
4. 第7场：候选马（第1组的2-3名 + 第2组的1-2名 + 第3组的1名）跑最后1场，取前2名

总共7场

title: 盲人分硬币（对称性）
answer:
1000枚硬币中980枚反面朝上、20枚正面朝上。蒙眼分成两堆使正面数相等。

答案：随机取20枚为一堆，将其全部翻转。

设取出的20枚中有m枚正面，则另一堆有(20-m)枚正面。翻转后第一堆的正面数变为(20-m)，与第二堆相等。
💡 翻转使正面↔反面，所以翻转后第一堆的正面数 = 翻转前的反面数 = 20-m = 另一堆的正面数。

title: 贴错标签的水果袋
answer:
三袋水果（苹果/橘子/混合），所有标签都贴错了。最少取几个水果才能确定？

答案：只需从"混合"标签的袋中取1个水果。

因为"混合"标签是错的，所以这袋要么全是苹果要么全是橘子。
• 若取出苹果 → "混合"袋是苹果 → "苹果"标签袋不能是苹果只能是混合 → "橘子"标签袋是橘子
• 若取出橘子 → 对称推理

💡 关键：利用"所有标签都错"这一约束，从"混合"标签入手（它不能是混合）。

title: 玻璃球坠楼（动态规划）
answer:
100层楼，2个玻璃球。球从≥X层扔会碎，
设最多扔N次。第一次从第N层扔：
• 碎了 → 用第2个球从1层逐层试，最多N-1次，总共N次
• 没碎 → 还有N-1次机会，从N+(N-1)层扔第二次

覆盖楼层数：N + (N-1) + ... + 1 = N(N+1)/2 ≥ 100
N = 14（14×15/2 = 105 ≥ 100）

策略：14 → 27 → 39 → 50 → 60 → 69 → 77 → 84 → 90 → 95 → 99 → 100

title: 囚徒帽子问题（模运算）
answer:
100个囚徒，每人戴红或蓝帽，能看到其他人的帽子但看不到自己的。按随机顺序猜测自己帽子颜色，猜错则死。

策略：至少救99人。

第一个囚徒数其他99人中红帽子的数量：
• 奇数 → 猜"红"
• 偶数 → 猜"蓝"

他有50%的生存率。之后每个人利用第一个人的信息 + 自己看到的其他98人的帽子颜色，推导出自己的颜色。
💡 推广到3种颜色：用模3运算，第一个囚徒报 sum % 3，仍有99人获救。

title: 彩球配色（马尔可夫链）
answer:
袋中20蓝球14红球。每次取两球：同色加蓝球，异色加红球。最后剩什么颜色？

分析红球数量的变化：
• 两蓝 → (B-1, R) → 红球不变
• 两红 → (B+1, R-2) → 红球-2
• 一红一蓝 → (B-1, R) → 红球不变

红球数要么不变要么-2，所以红球的奇偶性不变。
14是偶数 → 最后必为蓝球。若初始红球为奇数 → 最后为红球。

title: 配袜子（鸽巢原理）
answer:
抽屉有2红、20黄、31蓝袜子。随机抓几只保证有同色的一对？

3种颜色 = 3个鸽巢。由鸽巢原理，4只袜子（4只鸽子入3个洞）必有至少2只同色。
答案：4只

title: 假币称量II（三进制编码）
answer:
5袋硬币各100枚，每袋的币重为9g/10g/11g之一。用电子秤最少称几次确定每袋类型？

答案：只需1次。

从第i袋取 3^(i-1) 枚硬币一起称（即1, 3, 9, 27, 81枚）。

设标准重550g（55枚×10g），实际偏差为 ±(c₁×1 + c₂×3 + c₃×9 + c₄×27 + c₅×81)，其中cᵢ ∈ {-1, 0, 1}。

三进制表示的唯一性保证了不同的袋组合产生不同的总偏差，因此一次称量即可确定所有袋的类型。

title: 三个开关一个灯泡
answer:
房间外4个开关，房间内1个灯泡，只有1个开关控制灯泡。只能进房间1次，如何确定？

利用"热"这个额外信息：
1. 打开开关1和2，等待几分钟
2. 关闭开关2，打开开关3
3. 立即进入房间

• 灯亮且热 → 开关1
• 灯灭且热 → 开关2
• 灯亮且冷 → 开关3
• 灯灭且冷 → 开关4

title: 醉汉乘客（条件概率/对称性）
answer:
100人登机，第1人随机坐任何位置，其余人找自己座位被占则随机选。你是第100人，坐到自己座位的概率？

答案：50%

关键观察：最终只有两种可能——要么有人占了1号座（你能坐100号），要么有人占了100号座（你坐不了）。

在任何时候，下一个"随机选座"的人面对1号和100号座位的概率是对称的（相等）。所以最终1号和100号被占的概率各为1/2。

title: N个点在圆周上（连续概率）
answer:
在圆周上随机取N个点，它们全部落在某个半圆内的概率？

答案：N / 2^(N-1)

证明思路：
设事件Eᵢ = "从第i个点开始顺时针走半圈包含所有其他点"
• P(Eᵢ) = 1/2^(N-1)（每个其他点在半圆内的概率为1/2，相互独立）
• E₁, E₂, ..., E_N 互斥（不可能有两个点同时作为半圆起点包含所有其他点）

P(全部在半圆内) = Σ P(Eᵢ) = N / 2^(N-1)

title: 扑克牌概率
兔子跳台阶（斐波那契）
answer:
兔子在n级台阶底端，每次跳1或2级。到顶有多少种方式？

递推关系：f(n) = f(n-1) + f(n-2)

• f(1) = 1
• f(2) = 2（1+1 或 2）
• f(3) = 3, f(4) = 5, f(5) = 8...

这就是斐波那契数列！
💡 最后一步要么从n-1跳1级，要么从n-2跳2级。

title: 信封全错（容斥原理）
answer:
5封信随机放入5个信封，所有信都装错的概率？

用容斥原理：
P(至少1封正确) = ΣP(Eᵢ) - ΣP(EᵢEⱼ) + ΣP(EᵢEⱼEₖ) - ...

= C(5,1)×1/5 - C(5,2)×1/(5×4) + C(5,3)×1/(5×4×3) - ...
= 1 - 1/2! + 1/3! - 1/4! + 1/5!

P(全错) = 1 - P(至少1对) = 1/2! - 1/3! + 1/4! - 1/5! ≈ 36.8%
💡 一般公式：n封信全错的概率 = Σ(-1)^k / k! ≈ 1/e ≈ 36.79%

title: 蒙提霍尔问题（三门问题）
answer:
3扇门后1辆汽车2只羊。你选一扇门，主持人打开另一扇有羊的门，问你是否换门？

答案：应该换。换门后赢车概率2/3，不换1/3。

分析：
• 不换：你初始选对的概率 = 1/3
• 换：你初始选错的概率 = 2/3（主持人帮你排除了一个错误选项）

title: 男女比例问题
answer:
国家规定每家生到男孩就停，女孩继续生。最终男女比例？

答案：1:1

每次生育男孩和女孩概率各1/2，无论什么策略，总期望比例不变。

数学验证：n个家庭，期望男孩n个，期望女孩 = n×(1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + ...) = n个。
💡 停止策略不影响每次生育的性别概率。

title: 赌徒破产问题
answer:
赌徒有i元，每次以概率p赢1元或(1-p)输1元。目标到N元或0元停止。到达N的概率？

p = 1/2 时： P(到达N) = i/N

p ≠ 1/2 时：
P = [1 - (q/p)^i] / [1 - (q/p)^N], 其中 q = 1-p

💡 这是最经典的随机游走问题，用差分方程求解。

title: 收集优惠券问题
answer:
N种优惠券，每次随机获得一种（等概率）。收集齐全套平均需要多少张？

答案：N × H_N = N × (1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + ... + 1/N)

分析：
• 已有0种时，获得新种类概率1，期望1张
• 已有k种时，获得新种类概率(N-k)/N，期望N/(N-k)张

E[总张数] = Σ N/(N-k) = N × Σ 1/j = N × H_N

对于大N：E ≈ N × ln(N) + N × γ（γ ≈ 0.5772，欧拉常数）

title: 骰子游戏期望值
answer:
掷骰子：得4/5/6可以继续掷，得1/2/3停止。期望收益？

用全期望公式：

E[X] = P(Y∈{1,2,3}) × E[X|Y∈{1,2,3}] + P(Y∈{4,5,6}) × E[X|Y∈{4,5,6}]

= (1/2) × 2 + (1/2) × (5 + E[X])

E[X] = 1 + (5+E[X])/2 → E[X]/2 = 3.5 → E[X] = 7
💡 也可用Wald等式：E[N]=2, E[X]=3.5, E[SN]=E[X]×E[N]=7

title: 随机变量之和 < 1
answer:
X₁,...,Xₙ 独立同分布于U(0,1)。P(S=X₁+...+Xₙ < 1) = ?

答案：1/n!

归纳证明：
• n=1: P = 1 ✓
• n=2: 积分区域是三角形，面积1/2 ✓
• n=3: 四面体体积1/6 ✓

假设 P(Sₙ < 1) = 1/n!，则：
P(S_{n+1} < 1) = ∫ P(Sₙ < 1-x) dx = ∫ (1-x)ⁿ/n! dx = 1/(n+1)! ✓

title: 债券联合违约概率
500只蚂蚁（对称性/序统计量）
answer:
500只蚂蚁随机分布在1英尺绳上，各以1英尺/分钟匀速向随机方向移动。碰撞后掉头。所有蚂蚁落下的期望时间？

关键洞察：碰撞 = 标签交换
两蚂蚁碰撞掉头 = 它们穿过彼此继续走（标签交换）。所以忽略碰撞，每只蚂蚁独立。

期望时间 = max(500个U(0,1)随机变量的期望)
E[max] = n/(n+1) = 500/501 分钟

💡 这是"对称性思维"的经典应用——看似复杂的碰撞问题被简化为序统计量。

title: 看到第一张A的期望
answer:
52张牌中4张A。翻多少张牌平均能看到第一张A？

答案：10.6张

用指示变量法：
48张非A牌中，第i张在第一张A之前的概率 = 1/5（4张A将牌分成5个区域）

E[翻牌数] = 1 + Σ E[Xᵢ] = 1 + 48/5 = 10.6

💡 一般公式：m张普通牌+n张特殊牌，第一张特殊牌的位置期望 = 1 + m/(n+1)

title: 生日悖论
answer:
一个房间里至少多少人，有两个人生日相同的概率 > 50%？

答案：23人

P(全不同) = 365/365 × 364/365 × ... × (365-n+1)/365
当 n=23 时 P(至少1对相同) > 50%
当 n=50 时 P > 97%
当 n=70 时 P > 99.9%

💡 直觉上偏差大，因为比较的是"任意两人"而非"与某特定人"相同。配对数是C(n,2)。

title: 正面朝上概率（不公平硬币）
answer:
用一枚不公平硬币（P(正)=p未知）产生公平的二选一结果。

Von Neumann方法：每次掷两次
• 正反 → 选择1
• 反正 → 选择2
• 正正或反反 → 丢弃，重来

P(正反) = p(1-p) = P(反正)，所以两个结果等概率。
💡 期望需要的投掷次数 = 1/[2p(1-p)]

title: 连续掷出n个正面
answer:
公平硬币，期望掷多少次得到n个连续正面？

答案：2^(n+1) - 2

归纳法：
• n=1: E=2 ✓
• n=2: E=6 ✓
• n=3: E=14 ✓

递推：E[f(n+1)] = E[f(n)] + 1 + (1/2)×0 + (1/2)×E[f(n+1)]
→ E[f(n+1)] = 2×(E[f(n)] + 1) = 2^(n+2) - 2

title: e^π 与 π^e 哪个大
answer:
答案：e^π > π^e

取对数比较：e^π > π^e ⟺ π ln e > e ln π ⟺ ln e / e > ln π / π

考虑 f(x) = ln x / x，求导：
f'(x) = (1 - ln x) / x²

当 x > e 时 f'(x) < 0（递减）。由于 e < π，所以 f(e) > f(π)，即 ln e / e > ln π / π。

💡 另解：Taylor展开 e^x = 1+x+x²/2+... > 1+x，令x=π/e-1可得 e^(π/e) > π/e，即 e^π > π^e。

title: ln(x)的积分
answer:
∫ln(x)dx = ?

用分部积分：设u=ln x, v=x
∫ln(x)dx = x·ln(x) - ∫x·(1/x)dx = x·ln(x) - x + C

title: 标准正态的条件期望 E[X|X>0]
answer:
X ~ N(0,1)，求 E[X | X>0]。

E[X|X>0] = ∫₀^∞ x · f(x) dx / P(X>0)

其中 f(x) = (1/√2π) e^(-x²/2)

用换元 u = -x²/2, du = -x dx：
∫₀^∞ x e^(-x²/2) dx = ∫₀^(-∞) -e^u du = [e^u]₋∞⁰ = 1

E[X|X>0] = (1/√2π × 1) / (1/2) = √(2/π) ≈ 0.798

title: 高斯积分 ∫e^(-x²/2)dx
answer:
计算 ∫₋∞^∞ e^(-x²/2) dx

设 I = ∫₋∞^∞ e^(-x²/2) dx，则：
I² = ∫∫ e^(-(x²+y²)/2) dx dy

转换为极坐标 (x = r cosθ, y = r sinθ)：
I² = ∫₀^(2π) ∫₀^∞ e^(-r²/2) r dr dθ
= 2π × [e^(-r²/2)]₋... = 2π × 1 = 2π

I = √(2π)
💡 这就是正态分布归一化常数的由来。

title: L'Hôpital法则应用
answer:
求 lim(x→∞) eˣ/x² 和 lim(x→0⁺) x²ln(x)

第一个：∞/∞型，用L'Hôpital两次
lim eˣ/x² = lim eˣ/(2x) = lim eˣ/2 = ∞

第二个：改写为 ln(x) / (1/x²)，即 -∞/∞ 型
lim [ln(x) / x⁻²] = lim [1/x / (-2x⁻³)] = lim [-x²/2] = 0

title: 相关系数的范围（正定矩阵约束）
answer:
x与y相关0.8，x与z相关0.8。y与z相关系数范围？

方法一（向量夹角）：
cos θ = 0.8, 最小夹角2θ → ρ_min = cos(2θ) = 2cos²θ - 1 = 2(0.64) - 1 = 0.28
最大相关 = 1（同方向）

方法二（正定约束）：
相关矩阵的行列式 ≥ 0：
det = 1 - 0.64 - 0.64 - ρ² + 2(0.64)ρ ≥ 0
→ -0.28 + 1.28ρ - ρ² ≥ 0 → ρ ∈ [0.28, 1]

title: Cholesky分解生成相关正态变量
answer:
如何用独立N(0,1)生成相关系数ρ的两个标准正态变量？

X₁ = Z₁
X₂ = ρZ₁ + √(1-ρ²) Z₂


验证：
• Var(X₁) = Var(Z₁) = 1 ✓
• Var(X₂) = ρ² + (1-ρ²) = 1 ✓
• Cov(X₁,X₂) = Cov(Z₁, ρZ₁) = ρ ✓

💡 这是Cholesky分解的最简形式。对于n维，分解协方差矩阵Σ = RᵀR，然后X = μ + RᵀZ。

title: 最小二乘回归的矩阵推导
answer:
如何用矩阵方法推导线性回归的OLS估计量？

模型：Y = Xβ + ε
目标：min ||Y - Xβ||²

对β求导：
∂/∂β [(Y-Xβ)ᵀ(Y-Xβ)] = -2Xᵀ(Y-Xβ) = 0

→ XᵀXβ = XᵀY → β̂ = (XᵀX)⁻¹XᵀY

实际计算中可用QR分解：X = QR → β̂ = R⁻¹QᵀY，避免直接求逆的数值不稳定。
💡 OLS的5个假设：线性、零均值、同方差/不相关、无完全共线性、外生性。

title: Lagrange乘数法：点到平面距离
answer:
求原点到平面 2x+3y+4z=12 的距离。

min f = x²+y²+z², s.t. g = 2x+3y+4z-12 = 0

∇f = λ∇g:
2x = 2λ, 2y = 3λ, 2z = 4λ
→ x = λ, y = 3λ/2, z = 2λ

代入约束：2λ + 9λ/2 + 8λ = 12 → λ = 24/29
D = √(x²+y²+z²) = √[(24/29)² + (36/29)² + (48/29)²] = 12/√29

💡 一般公式：点(a₀,b₀,c₀)到平面 ax+by+cz=d 的距离 = |d-aa₀-bb₀-cc₀| / √(a²+b²+c²)

title: 醉汉走桥（鞅论）
answer:
醉汉在100米桥的17米处，每步等概率前进/后退1米。到100米先于0米的概率？到达任一端的期望步数？

设当前位置为0，对称随机游走停在a=83或-β=-17。

Sₙ和Sₙ²-n都是鞅，停止时刻的鞅仍为鞅。

E[S_N] = pₐ × 83 + (1-pₐ) × (-17) = 0 → pₐ = 17/100 = 0.17

E[Sₙ² - N] = 0 → E[N] = pₐ × 83² + (1-pₐ) × 17² = 1441步
💡 一般公式：停在a或-β的概率分别为β/(α+β)和α/(α+β)，期望步数αβ。

title: 售票问题（反射原理）
answer:
2n人排队买票，n人持$5、n人持$10，票价$5，售票员无零钱。所有人都能顺利买票的概率？

答案：1/(n+1)

思路：将持$5的人映射为+1，持$10的人映射为-1，问题变为：从(0,0)到(2n,0)的随机游走中，不触及y=-1的概率。

用反射原理：触及y=-1的路径数 = 从(0,-2)到(2n,0)的路径数 = C(2n, n-1)

不触及的路径数 = C(2n,n) - C(2n,n-1) = C(2n,n)/(n+1)

P = [C(2n,n)/(n+1)] / C(2n,n) = 1/(n+1)（卡特兰数相关）

title: 硬币三连（Penney's Game）
answer:
公平硬币，玩家A先选3连序列，B后选。谁的序列先出现谁赢。

关键：B总能选到胜率>50%的序列！

策略：取A序列的后两位的反序列作为B序列的前两位。

例如A选HHH → B选THH，B胜率7/8
A选HTH → B选HHT，B胜率2/3

💡 这说明三连序列的胜负关系是非传递的（类似石头剪刀布）。B的最优策略保证至少2/3胜率。

title: Brown运动定义与性质
answer:
定义：连续随机过程W(t), t≥0满足：
1. W(0) = 0
2. 增量独立：W(t₂)-W(t₁), W(t₃)-W(t₂), ... 相互独立
3. W(t+s)-W(t) ~ N(0, s)

重要性质：
• 连续（无跳跃）
• E[W(t)] = 0, E[W(t)²] = t
• 鞅性：E[W(t+s)|W(t)] = W(t)
• Cov(W(s), W(t)) = min(s,t)
• Markov性（连续空间）

两个重要鞅：
• W(t)² - t 是鞅
• exp{λW(t) - λ²t/2} 是鞅（指数鞅）

title: Brown运动停时的期望
answer:
B(t)首次到达±1的平均时间？

用鞅论：B(t)²-t是鞅

设T = min{t : B(t)=1或B(t)=-1}

由Ito引理：d(B²-t) = 2B dB，无drift项 → 鞅

E[B(T)²-T] = E[B(0)²-0] = 0
E[B(T)²] = 1（停在±1）

→ E[T] = 1

💡 一般情况：停在a或-β的期望时间 = αβ（与离散情况一致！）

title: B(t)>0且B(2)<0的概率
answer:
标准Brown运动 B₁>0 且 B₂<0 的概率？

答案：1/8

B₁ ~ N(0,1), B₂-B₁ ~ N(0,1) 独立

B₁>0, B₂<0 ⟺ B₁>0, B₂-B₁ < -B₁

用对称性：将(B₁, B₂-B₁)的密度函数空间分成8个等概率区域（由x=0, y=0, y=x, y=-x分割），目标区域占1/8。

title: 动态骰子游戏
answer:
掷骰子：1-5各得对应金额，6则失去所有累积奖金。每次掷后可选停或继续。最多愿付多少？

用动态规划求解：

当累积n元时，继续掷的期望：
(n+1)/6 + (n+2)/6 + ... + (n+5)/6 + 0/6 = 5n/6 + 2.5

当 5n/6 + 2.5 > n 时继续，即 n ≤ 14

递推计算 f(15)=15, f(14)=14.17, ..., f(0) = 6.15
💡 愿意为游戏最多支付 $6.15。

title: 动态纸牌游戏（最优停时）
answer:
52张牌(26红26黑)，逐张翻开，红+1黑-1。可随时叫停，求最优策略和期望收益。

动态规划方程：
f(b,r) = max(b-r, b/(b+r)×f(b-1,r) + r/(b+r)×f(b,r-1))

边界条件：f(0,r)=0, f(b,0)=b

答案：f(26,26) = $2.62

💡 这个方程本质上就是美式期权的定价方程——在最优时间行权。

title: 期权价格的影响因素
answer:
欧式/美式期权价格随各变量变化方向：

变量欧式Call美式Call欧式Put美式Put
股价S↑↑↑↓↓
行权价K↑↓↓↑↑
到期时间τ↑?↑?↑
波动率σ↑↑↑↑↑
无风险利率r↑↑↑↓↓
股息D↑↓↓↑↑

💡 欧式期权的到期时间影响不确定，因为中间可能有股息发放。

title: Put-Call Parity（看涨看跌平价）
answer:
欧式期权看涨看跌平价：
c + Ke^(-rτ) = p + S - D

证明（无套利）：

组合A：1份Call + 面值K的零息债券 → 到期T收益 = max(S_T, K)
组合B：1份Put + 1股股票 → 到期T收益 = max(S_T, K)

两组合到期收益相同 → 当前价值必须相同 → c + Ke^(-rτ) = p + S - D

💡 由此可得：S-D-Ke^(-rτ) ≤ c ≤ S（无套利边界）。美式期权则是不等式关系。

title: 为什么不在到期前行使美式看涨期权（无股息）
answer:
无股息股票的美式Call = 欧式Call，提前行使永远不是最优的。

论据1（时间价值）：c = (S-K) + (K-Ke^(-rτ)) + p > S-K = 内含价值。出售期权比行使更划算。

论据2（替代策略）：不行使，而是卖空股票+借出K。到期时无论ST如何，都有正收益：
T时刻收益 = Ke^(rτ) - S_T > 0 （当S_T>K时）


论据3（Jensen不等式）：Call收益是凸函数，E[e^(-rτ)C(S_T)] ≥ C(E^Q[S_T]) = C(Se^(rτ)) → 等待更优。

💡 但美式Put不同！P(0)=K≠0，所以 Jensen 论据不成立，提前行使可能最优。

title: Black-Scholes-Merton微分方程
answer:
基于无套利和Δ对冲推导BSM方程：

构建组合Π = -f + (∂f/∂S)×S（卖空1份衍生品+买入Δ股股票）

由Ito引理：
df = (∂f/∂t + ½σ²S²∂²f/∂S²)dt + ∂f/∂S × dS


对冲后dΠ = (∂f/∂t + ½σ²S²∂²f/∂S²)dt（消除dS项）

无套利 → dΠ = rΠdt → BSM方程：
∂f/∂t + rS∂f/∂S + ½σ²S²∂²f/∂S² = rf

title: Black-Scholes公式
answer:
欧式Call和Put的BS定价公式：

c = S₀e^(-yτ) N(d₁) - Ke^(-rτ) N(d₂)
p = Ke^(-rτ) N(-d₂) - S₀e^(-yτ) N(-d₁)


其中：
d₁ = [ln(S₀/K) + (r-y+σ²/2)τ] / (σ√τ)
d₂ = d₁ - σ√τ


各参数含义：
• N(d₂) = 风险中性下Call被行使的概率
• N(d₁) = Delta（对冲比率）
• S₀e^(-yτ)N(d₁) = 风险中性期望的股票部分
• Ke^(-rτ)N(d₂) = 行权价的贴现期望

title: Delta的对冲含义
answer:
Delta = ∂c/∂S = e^(-yτ)N(d₁)

Delta的性质：
• Call的Delta ∈ (0, 1)：股价涨，Call涨
• Put的Delta ∈ (-1, 0)：股价涨，Put跌
• ATM附近 Delta ≈ 0.5（Call）
• 深度实值Call → Delta → 1
• 深度虚值Call → Delta → 0

Delta中性对冲：持有Δ份股票对冲1份空头Call，使组合在小区间内对股价不敏感。

title: Bull Spread（牛市价差）
answer:
买入低行权价K₁的Call + 卖出高行权价K₂的Call（K₂>K₁）。

收益结构：
• S_T ≤ K₁：收益 = 0
• K₁ < S_T < K₂：收益 = S_T - K₁
• S_T ≥ K₂：收益 = K₂ - K₁（封顶）

特点：降低权利金成本，但牺牲了大涨的收益。看涨但认为涨幅有限时使用。

title: Straddle（跨式）
answer:
买入同行权价同到期日的Call + Put。

收益结构：收益 = |S_T - K| - 权利金

适用场景：预期价格大幅波动但不确定方向（如财报前、重大事件前）。

盈亏平衡点： K ± (Call+Put权利金)
💡 反向操作（卖出Straddle）则赌价格不动，风险无限。

title: 二值期权（Binary Option）
answer:
到期时S_T > K 则支付$1，否则$0。

定价（风险中性）：
价格 = e^(-rτ) × P^Q(S_T > K) = e^(-rτ) × N(d₂)


其中 d₂ = [ln(S₀/K) + (r-y-σ²/2)τ] / (σ√τ)

💡 二值期权的Delta在接近到期且接近平值时会变得极大（接近无穷），风险很高。

title: VaR（Value at Risk）
answer:
在置信度α下，投资组合在持有期Δt内的最大可能损失。

参数法（正态假设）：
VaR_α = μ + z_α × σ

z_α为标准正态的α分位数（如95%置信度z=1.645）

历史模拟法：用历史收益分布直接取分位数
蒙特卡洛法：模拟未来收益路径取分位数

💡 VaR的缺陷：不度量尾部厚度，不满足次可加性。ES (Expected Shortfall) 更优。

title: 久期与凸性
answer:
久期（Duration）：债券价格对利率的一阶敏感度
D = -(1/P) × dP/dy ≈ 价格变动/利率变动


修正久期：D_mod = D / (1+y/m)

凸性（Convexity）：二阶敏感度
C = (1/P) × d²P/dy²


价格近似：ΔP/P ≈ -D_mod × Δy + ½C × (Δy)²

💡 久期衡量线性风险，凸性修正非线性部分。凸性越大，利率变化时获益/损失越不对称（利好）。

title: 利率模型概述
answer:
常见短期利率模型：

1. Vasicek模型：dr = a(b-r)dt + σdW
均值回归，但利率可能为负

2. CIR模型：dr = a(b-r)dt + σ√r dW
均值回归且利率≥0（当r→0时波动率→0）

3. Ho-Lee模型：dr = θ(t)dt + σdW
无套利模型，θ(t)匹配初始期限结构

4. Hull-White模型：dr = a(b(t)-r)dt + σdW
Vasicek的时变参数版本

title: 不用临时变量交换两个数
answer:
方法1（加减法）：
a = a + b; b = a - b; a = a - b;

方法2（异或）：
a = a ^ b; b = a ^ b; a = a ^ b;

💡 异或法更安全（不会溢出），但可读性差。

title: Horner算法求多项式
answer:
计算 p(x) = aₙxⁿ + ... + a₁x + a₀。

朴素方法：逐项算 xᵏ 再乘系数，O(n²) 次乘法。
Horner 算法（秦九韶）：嵌套形式 p(x) = ((...(aₙx + aₙ₋₁)x + ...)x + a₁)x + a₀，只需 O(n) 次乘法与加法。

result = a[n];
for (i = n-1; i >= 0; i--)
result = result * x + a[i];

本质：从最高次系数开始，每一步"乘 x 加下一项系数"。

title: 100个储物柜开关
answer:
100个储物柜初始关闭，第i轮翻转所有编号为i倍数的柜门（i=1..100）。最后哪些开着？

编号为n的柜门被翻转的次数 = n的约数个数。
只有完全平方数有奇数个约数（约数成对，平方数有一个重复）。

答案：编号为1,4,9,16,...,100（共10个完全平方数）的柜门最后开着。

title: 木棍上的蚂蚁
answer:
一根长1米的木棍上有N只蚂蚁，各以1cm/s随机向左或向右爬，相遇则掉头。问所有蚂蚁掉下木棍的最长时间？

关键技巧：相遇掉头 ≡ 互相穿过（蚂蚁不可区分）。
因此最长时间 = 最远的蚂蚁到端点的最大距离 = 1米（100秒）。
💡 把'掉头'替换为'穿过'，问题立刻简化。

title: 天平找假币（9球1重）
answer:
9个外观相同的球，其中1个略重，用无砝码天平2次找出。怎么称？

分3组(1-3)(4-6)(7-9)。
第1次称(1-3) vs (4-6)：
• 平衡→坏球在7-9，第2次称7 vs 8即可定位
• 偏重→坏球在偏重那组，第2次称组内两个即可

3次称量最多可从3ⁿ个球中找出已知方向的坏球；n=2覆盖9个。

title: 狼、羊、白菜过河
answer:
人带狼、羊、白菜过河，船每次只能载人和一样东西。狼吃羊、羊吃菜（人不在时）。如何全过河？

1. 带羊过去，空船回
2. 带狼过去，带羊回
3. 带菜过去，空船回
4. 带羊过去

共7趟。（关键：绝不单独留狼+羊或羊+菜）

title: 蒙提霍尔三门问题
answer:
三扇门后一车两羊。你选1号，主持人（知情）打开一扇有羊的门（如3号）。问：换选2号是否更有利？

换选胜率2/3，不换1/3。
你初选对的概率1/3；若对则换输，若错(2/3)则换赢。主持人揭示信息后，换选把'初选错'的2/3概率收归己有。

title: 水壶问题（3升和5升得4升）
answer:
只用3升和5升无刻度水壶，如何恰好得到4升水？

法一：5满→倒满3（剩2）→倒空3→把2倒入3→5满→倒满3（需1）→5中剩4。
法二：3满×2倒入5（5中有6? 不行）。用法一即可。

title: 变色龙问题
answer:
13只红、15只绿、17只蓝变色龙。相遇时若颜色不同则都变成第三种颜色。能否最终全同色？

考虑数量模3：
红-绿 ≡ 13-15 ≡ -2 ≡ 1 (mod3)；绿-蓝 ≡ 15-17 ≡ -2 ≡1；蓝-红≡17-13≡1。
每次相遇使两种颜色±1、第三种颜色±2，任意两色之差 mod3 不变。
全同色要求某两色差为0 mod3，但初始差均≡1 mod3 → 不可能。

title: 两列火车与飞鸟
answer:
A、B两城相距100km，两车各以50km/h相向开。一只鸟以75km/h在两车间来回飞，直到相撞。鸟飞了多远？

两车相遇时间 = 100/100 = 1小时。
鸟一直飞：距离 = 75 × 1 = 75km。
💡 别算无穷级数，算'总时间×速度'。

title: 骆驼运香蕉
answer:
沙漠3000根香蕉，骆驼每次最多驮1000根，每走1km吃1根。最远能运多少到1000km外的市场？

分段驮运：
• 前200km需往返3趟→耗5根/km，到200km处剩2000根
• 再333.3km需往返2趟→耗3根/km，到533.3km处剩1000根
• 最后466.7km单趟→耗1根/km
剩余 = 1000 - 466.7 = 约533根。

title: 烧香计时75分钟
answer:
两根不均匀香各烧1小时。如何量出75分钟？

先点A两端+B一端（30min后A尽），同时点C？只有两根：
30min时A尽，B剩30min量，立刻点B另一端→15min尽，合计45min（得45）。
75分钟做法：A两端+B一端起；A尽(30)点B另端→B再15尽(45)；此时重新点第二根香？需第三根。
两根香最多得45/30分钟；75分钟需3根香。

title: 连续抛硬币到HH的期望次数
answer:
独立抛公平硬币，直到首次出现连续两个正面(HH)，求期望抛多少次？

设E为期望。状态：E0(无前导H)、E1(末尾一个H)。
E0 = 1 + ½E0 + ½E1；E1 = 1 + ½·0 + ½E0（抛H成功结束，抛T回E0）。
解得 E0 = 6。对比HT期望=4（不对称）。

title: 错排问题（帽子检查）
answer:
n个人把帽子随机放回，求'没人拿到自己帽子'的概率（当n→∞）？

错排数 !n = n!·Σ_{k=0}^n (-1)^k/k!。
概率 = !n/n! = Σ_{k=0}^n (-1)^k/k! → 1/e ≈ 0.3679。

title: 两个骰子点数之和的期望最大值
生日悖论（23人）
赠券收集者（Coupon Collector）
answer:
集齐n种优惠券，每次随机得一种，求集齐的期望次数？

第k种缺时，获得新券概率(n-k+1)/n，期望 n/(n-k+1)。
总期望 = n·H_n = n(1+½+...+1/n) ≈ n ln n + γn。

title: 三门之后：两个信封
answer:
两信封各装一笔钱，一个正好是另一个的两倍。你随机选一个打开见$100，可否换得更多？

经典悖论：换的期望 = ½·50 + ½·200 = 125 > 100，似乎应换；但对称性说明'换总有利'矛盾。
破解：'另一封是50或200各½'的先验不成立——需知道金额分布；无分布时无法定优劣。

title: 伯特兰盒子悖论
answer:
三盒：MM、NN、MN各一枚（金/银币）。随机取盒再随机取一币，是金。另一枚也是金的概率？

金币共3枚：MM盒2枚、MN盒1枚。取到金币时，它来自MM盒的概率2/3。
答案：2/3（不是1/2——金币不等可能来自各盒）。

title: 赌徒破产概率
answer:
赌徒有$i，目标$N，每局赢1概率p输1概率q=1-p。求到达N（而非破产）的概率？

p≠q时：P_i = (1-(q/p)^i)/(1-(q/p)^N)。
p=q=½时：P_i = i/N。

title: 两随机整数乘积为偶的概率
answer:
从1..n独立随机取两整数，乘积为偶数的概率？

乘积为奇 ⇔ 两数皆奇。P(奇)= (⌈n/2⌉/n)²。
n为偶时 = (½)² = ¼，故P(偶)= 3/4。

title: 圆周上随机两点
answer:
在圆周上独立随机取两点，弦长超过半径的概率？

固定一点，另一点需落在距其弧长<60°的弧外（弦长>半径对应圆心角<60°）。
P(弦长>半径)=1 - 60/180 = 2/3。

title: 疾病检测（贝叶斯）
answer:
某病患病率1%，检测对病患95%阳性、对健康95%阴性（假阳5%）。检测阳性，真患病概率？

P(病|阳)= 0.01·0.95 / (0.01·0.95 + 0.99·0.05) ≈ 0.0095/0.058 = ≈16.1%。
💡 基础率很低时，阳性大概率假阳。

title: x^x 的导数
answer:
求 f(x)=x^x (x>0) 的导数。

取对数：ln f = x ln x；两边求导 f'/f = ln x + 1。
f' = x^x (ln x + 1)。

title: 高斯积分 ∫e^{-x²}dx
answer:
求 ∫_{-∞}^{∞} e^{-x²} dx。

令 I² = ∫∫ e^{-(x²+y²)} dxdy，转极坐标：=∫_0^{2π}∫_0^∞ e^{-r²} r dr dθ = π。
故 I = √π。

title: 极限 (1+1/n)^n
answer:
证明 lim_{n→∞}(1+1/n)^n = e。并给出 e^x 的泰勒展开。

由 ln(1+1/n)→0 与展开可得极限为e。
e^x = Σ_{k=0}^∞ x^k/k! = 1 + x + x²/2 + x³/6 + ...（对任意x收敛）。

title: 矩阵 [[2,1],[1,2]] 的特征值
answer:
求矩阵 A=[[2,1],[1,2]] 的特征值与特征向量。

det(A-λI)=(2-λ)²-1=λ²-4λ+3=0 → λ=1,3。
λ=1: 特征向量(1,-1)ᵀ；λ=3: 特征向量(1,1)ᵀ。

title: ∫ 1/(1+x²) dx 与 arctan
answer:
求不定积分 ∫ 1/(1+x²) dx，并算 ∫_0^1。

∫ 1/(1+x²) dx = arctan x + C。
∫_0^1 = arctan 1 - 0 = π/4。

title: 函数 f=x²+y² 的梯度
answer:
求 f(x,y)=x²+y² 的梯度，并说明其在(1,1)处的方向。

∇f = (2x, 2y)。在(1,1)为(2,2)，指向径向向外，是上升最快方向。

title: 矩阵迹等于特征值之和
answer:
证明：对任意方阵，tr(A)=特征值之和；det(A)=特征值之积。

特征多项式 p(λ)=det(λI-A)=λⁿ - tr(A)λⁿ⁻¹ + ... + (-1)ⁿ det(A)。
其根为特征值，由韦达定理：tr(A)=Σλ_i，det(A)=Πλ_i。

title: 解常微分方程 dX/dt=aX
answer:
解 dX/dt = aX，初值X(0)=X0。并推广到 dS/S = μdt+σdW（几何布朗）。

确定情形：X(t)=X0 e^{at}。
随机情形（Itô）：S(t)=S0 exp((μ-σ²/2)t + σW_t)。

title: 秩与线性无关
answer:
什么是矩阵的秩？秩为r意味着什么？

秩 = 列（或行）向量组的极大线性无关组大小 = 行阶梯形非零行数。
rank(AB) ≤ min(rank A, rank B)；满秩方阵可逆。

title: 看跌-看涨平价（Put-Call Parity）
answer:
写出欧式期权看跌-看涨平价关系，并说明用途。

C - P = S - K e^{-rT}（无分红）。
用途：由任三者可推第四个；构造合成头寸（如合成多头 = 买C + 卖P + 借K e^{-rT}）。

title: Black-Scholes 看涨公式
answer:
写出欧式看涨期权 BSM 定价公式。

C = S N(d1) - K e^{-rT} N(d2)，
d1=(ln(S/K)+(r+σ²/2)T)/(σ√T)，d2=d1-σ√T。
N(·)为标准正态CDF。

title: Delta 的含义与近似
answer:
期权Delta是什么？认沽/认购Delta范围？

Delta = ∂C/∂S，标的涨1元期权约涨Δ元。
认购Delta∈(0,1)；认沽Delta∈(-1,0)。平值≈0.5。

title: 远期价格公式
answer:
无分红资产远期价格F如何确定？若F≠理论值会怎样？

F = S e^{rT}（无套利，借S买标的持有至T成本=S e^{rT}）。
若市价>F则卖出远期+买入现货套利；若

title: 一步二叉树定价
answer:
用一步二叉树为欧式看涨定价（上涨u、下跌d、风险中性概率p）。

p=(e^{rΔt}-d)/(u-d)，C = e^{-rΔt}[p·max(Su-K,0)+(1-p)·max(Sd-K,0)]。
风险中性下期望贴现即价格。

title: 隐含波动率
answer:
什么是隐含波动率？为什么它常被报而非价格？

把市价反代入BSM解出的σ即隐含波动率。
它把价格'标准化'便于比较不同行权价/期限；'波动率微笑'反映模型缺陷（假设常数σ不成立）。

title: 美式 vs 欧式（分红影响）
answer:
为何美式期权通常比欧式贵？分红股票的美式看涨可能提前行权吗？

美式可提前行权→更多权利→价格≥欧式。
无分红时美式看涨=欧式（提前行权不优）；有分红时可能提前行权以 capture 分红。

title: Delta 对冲直觉
answer:
Delta中性组合如何构建与再平衡？

卖1份看涨，买Δ股标的→组合对S一阶不敏感。
S变动后Δ变，需再交易使组合回中性——'动态对冲'，频率越高复制越准（理论连续→BSM）。

title: CAPM 期望收益
answer:
写出CAPM公式并解释β。无风险利率3%、市场溢价5%、β=1.2，期望收益？

E[R_i]=R_f + β_i(E[R_m]-R_f)。
β衡量系统性风险。代入：3%+1.2×5%=9%。

title: 用错价期权套利
answer:
市场看涨价C*高于理论C，如何无风险套利？

卖出贵Call C*，同时买入合成看涨（买标的S+卖Put P+借K e^{-rT}，成本=C），锁定 C*-C>0。
到期对冲平仓，稳赚价差。

title: 布朗运动的四条性质
answer:
布朗运动 W_t 有哪些基本性质？

1) W_0=0；2) 连续路径；3) 独立增量；4) W_t-W_s ~ N(0, t-s)。
由此 E[W_t]=0，Var(W_t)=t。

title: Itô 引理
answer:
陈述 Itô 引理（对 f(t, W_t)）。

df = (∂f/∂t + ½ σ² ∂²f/∂x²) dt + (∂f/∂x) dW（设dx=μdt+σdW）。
比普通链式法则多½σ²f''项（二阶项不能忽略）。

title: 鞅的定义
answer:
什么是鞅（martingale）？给一个例子。

E[X_t | F_s]=X_s (s布朗运动W_t、E[W_t|F_s]=W_s 是鞅；W_t²-t也是鞅（Itô）。

title: 几何布朗运动 SDE
answer:
资产价格常用什么模型？写出SDE并解。

dS = μS dt + σS dW（几何布朗）。
由Itô：S_t = S_0 exp((μ-σ²/2)t + σW_t)。对数收益~N((μ-σ²/2)t, σ²t)。

title: 布朗运动的二次变差
answer:
Brownian motion 的二次变差 [W,W]_t = ? 含义？

对划分 Σ(W_{t_i}-W_{t_{i-1}})² → t（依概率）。
对比光滑函数二次变差为0——这是布朗'粗糙'的体现，也是Itô积分与黎曼积分的根本区别。

title: 泊松过程
answer:
强度λ的泊松过程，到达间隔分布？t内k次到达概率？

间隔 i.i.d. ~ Exp(λ)；P(N_t=k)= (λt)^k e^{-λt}/k!。
E[N_t]=λt，Var=λt。

title: Ornstein-Uhlenbeck 过程
answer:
写出OU过程及其均值回复特性。

dX = θ(μ-X)dt + σ dW。
长期均值回归到μ；平稳分布~N(μ, σ²/(2θ))。常用于利率/波动率建模。

title: Itô 等距 / Itô 积分是鞅
answer:
为何 Itô 积分 ∫_0^t H_s dW_s 是鞅？

在适应且平方可积条件下，Itô等距 E[(∫H dW)²]=E[∫H² ds]，且 E[∫H dW | F_s]=∫_0^s H dW。
故随机积分本身是无漂移鞅——这是风险中性定价基石。

title: 二分查找的复杂度
answer:
对已排序数组二分查找，时间/空间复杂度？前提？

时间 O(log n)，空间O(1)（迭代）。
前提：数组有序；每次折半区间。

title: 归并排序复杂度
answer:
归并排序的时间与空间复杂度？稳定吗？

时间始终 O(n log n)（最好/最坏）；空间O(n)（辅助数组）。
稳定。分治典型。

title: 快速排序复杂度
answer:
快排平均与最坏时间？如何避免最坏？

平均 O(n log n)；最坏（已排序且选端）O(n²)。
随机化选 pivot 或三数取中→几乎总O(n log n)。最坏空间O(log n)。

title: 检测链表环（Floyd）
answer:
如何判断单链表有环？复杂度？

快慢指针：快走2步、慢走1步，相遇则有环。
时间O(n)，空间O(1)。相遇点再定位可求环入口。

title: Two Sum
answer:
给定数组与target，找两数和为target的下标。最优做法？

哈希表存'值→下标'，遍历时查 target-x 是否已在表中。
时间O(n)，空间O(n)。

title: Kadane 最大子数组
answer:
求数组最大连续子数组和，时间O(n)做法？

维护 cur=max(x, cur+x)，ans=max(ans,cur)。
一次遍历：O(n)。负全时返回最大（最小负）元素。

title: Fisher-Yates 洗牌
answer:
如何均匀随机打乱数组？为什么不能'对每个位置随机选任一位置'？

从尾到头，位置i与[0,i]随机交换。每个排列等概率。
若每次与[0,n-1]交换则分布不均（nⁿ种≠n!排列）。

title: BFS 与 DFS 区别
answer:
图的BFS与DFS各自适合什么？复杂度？

均 O(V+E)。BFS求最短路径（无权）、层序；DFS探路径/拓扑/连通分量。
BFS用队列，DFS用栈/递归。

title: 汉诺塔递推
answer:
n盘汉诺塔最少移动次数？递归思路？

T(n)=2T(n-1)+1 → T(n)=2ⁿ-1。
把n-1盘移到辅助柱，移最大盘，再移回。

title: 堆求数据流中位数
answer:
如何O(log n)插入、O(1)取中位数维护数据流？

两个堆：大顶堆存较小半、小顶堆存较大半，保持大小差≤1。
中位数=堆顶之一（或平均）。插入O(log n)。

title: 骑士与无赖（Knights & Knaves）
answer:
岛上骑士只说真话、无赖只说假话。A说'我们俩都是无赖'。A、B各是谁？

假设A是骑士→其话为真→两人都是无赖，与'A是骑士'矛盾，故A不可能是骑士。
所以A是无赖→其话为假→'并非两人都是无赖'→至少有一人是骑士→B是骑士。
答案：A是无赖，B是骑士。

title: 两守卫两门
answer:
两门一宝一虎，两守卫一总真一总假，只能问一句。怎么问知宝门？

问任一守卫：'另一个守卫会说哪扇是宝门？'然后选相反的。
真守卫会转述假的（指向虎门），假守卫也会指向虎门→总得虎门，取反即宝门。

title: 称球逻辑（信息论下界）
answer:
12球1异（不知轻重），天平3次能找出，信息论下界为何是3次？

可能状态 12×2=24 种。每次称量3结果→3次覆盖3³=27≥24。
2次仅9<24不够→至少3次。

title: 三个开关与灯泡（接上一题变体）
answer:
房间外3开关控1灯泡，进房1次判定。用'热'解决（见上）。若只允许看亮灭（不看热）还需几开关？

仅看亮灭时2态/次，1灯泡最多区分2状态→只能定位1个开关；3开关需额外信息（热/声音）。

title: 说谎者悖论
answer:
'这句话是假的'为何是悖论？它在逻辑系统中说明什么？

若真则假，若假则真，无一致真值。
说明朴素自指会导致不一致，推动了塔斯基真值分层、哥德尔不完备等理论。

title: 毒酒问题（信息论）
answer:
1000桶酒1桶毒，用最少的老鼠（喝后次日死）找出毒桶，要几只？

每只老鼠 binary：喝/不喝。n只老鼠可区分2ⁿ桶。
2¹⁰=1024≥1000 → 10只（按二进制编码每桶对应老鼠组合）。

title: 移动平均的高效计算
answer:
计算大小为k的滑动窗口平均值。

朴素方法：O(n×k)
高效方法：O(n)

sum = sum(arr[0:k]);
for (i = k; i < n; i++) {
sum += arr[i] - arr[i-k];
avg = sum / k;
}

💡 每次只加上新元素减去旧元素，避免重复求和。

title: 随机排列（Fisher-Yates）
answer:
生成1到n的随机排列。

Fisher-Yates洗牌算法（O(n)）：
for (i = n-1; i > 0; i--) {
j = rand(0, i);
swap(arr[i], arr[j]);
}

正确性：每个位置等概率地被分配到剩余位置中的任意一个，保证所有n!种排列等概率出现。

title: 斐波那契数列
answer:
F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2), F(0)=0, F(1)=1

递归： O(2ⁿ) —— 太慢
动态规划： O(n) —— 空间O(n)或O(1)
矩阵快速幂： O(log n)

// 矩阵快速幂
[[F(n)], [F(n-1)]] = [[1,1],[1,0]]^(n-1) × [[1],[0]]

💡 通项公式：F(n) = (φⁿ - ψⁿ)/√5，其中φ=(1+√5)/2（黄金比）。

title: 最大连续子数组和（Kadane算法）
answer:
求数组中连续子数组的最大和。

Kadane算法 O(n)：
max_ending = arr[0]; max_so_far = arr[0];
for (i = 1; i < n; i++) {
max_ending = max(arr[i], max_ending + arr[i]);
max_so_far = max(max_so_far, max_ending);
}
return max_so_far;

关键思想：到位置i的最大和，要么包含i-1的最大和+arr[i]，要么只有arr[i]本身。
💡 变体：二维最大子矩阵、不允许全负的变种、返回子数组本身等。

title: 毒酒问题（信息论/二进制）
answer:
1000瓶酒中1瓶有毒，毒药24小时后发作。用最少老鼠在24小时内找出毒酒。

答案：10只老鼠。

方法：将1000瓶酒编号为1-1000(二进制最多10位)。
第j只老鼠喝所有第j位为1的酒。

24小时后，哪些老鼠死了构成一个10位二进制数，直接对应毒酒的编号。

⌈log₂(1000)⌉ = 10

💡 本质是信息论：1000种可能需要log₂1000 ≈ 10 bits信息，每只老鼠提供1 bit。

title: 蒙特卡洛模拟
answer:
用随机数模拟解决确定性问题。

基本步骤：
1. 定义输入变量的概率分布
2. 随机采样生成场景
3. 对每个场景计算输出
4. 统计输出分布

误差估计：
标准误差 = σ/√N

要将误差减半，需要4倍的样本量。

方差缩减技术：
• 对偶变量法（Antithetic variates）
• 控制变量法（Control variates）
• 重要性采样（Importance sampling）
• 分层采样（Stratified sampling）

title: 有限差分法
answer:
用差分近似微分方程，将PDE转化为线性方程组。

三种差分格式：
• 前向差分：f'(x) ≈ [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h （显式，有条件稳定）
• 后向差分：f'(x) ≈ [f(x) - f(x-h)] / h （隐式，无条件稳定）
• 中心差分：f'(x) ≈ [f(x+h) - f(x-h)] / (2h) （二阶精度）

Crank-Nicolson格式：
平均前向和后向差分 → 二阶精度且无条件稳定

💡 用于期权定价时，显式格式有稳定性条件 Δt ≤ Δx²/(2σ²)，隐式和CN无此限制。

title: C++虚函数与多态
answer:
虚函数（virtual function）实现运行时多态：

class Base {
virtual void foo() { cout << "Base"; }
};
class Derived : public Base {
void foo() override { cout << "Derived"; }
};
// Base* p = new Derived();
// p->foo(); // 输出 "Derived"

原理：每个含虚函数的类有虚函数表（vtable），对象中存储vtable指针。调用时通过vtable查找实际函数地址。

注意：
• 构造函数不能是虚函数
• 析构函数应为虚函数（避免内存泄漏）
• 虚函数有微小的运行时开销

title: 智能指针（C++11）
answer:
unique_ptr：独占所有权，不可拷贝，可移动
std::unique_ptr p(new T());

shared_ptr：共享所有权，引用计数
std::shared_ptr p = std::make_shared();

weak_ptr：不增加引用计数，解决shared_ptr循环引用
std::weak_ptr wp = sp;

💡 优先使用make_unique/make_shared而非直接new，可减少内存泄漏和提高性能。

title: 两扇门与两个守卫
answer:
两扇门：一扇通向offer，一扇通向出口。两个守卫：一个总说真话，一个总说假话。只能问一个是非问题。

问："另一个守卫会说你守卫的是通向offer的门吗？"

• 回答"是" → 选另一扇门
• 回答"否" → 选这扇门

分析：
情景1：真话守卫在offer门前 → 假话守卫会说"否" → 真话守卫如实转述"否"
情景2：假话守卫在offer门前 → 真话守卫会说"是" → 假话守卫谎称"否"

两种情景下回答都是"否"，所以"否"→选此门，"是"→选另一扇。

title: 安全传递文件（密码学思维）
answer:
你需要通过不可靠快递向同事发送机密文件。你们各有自己的锁和唯一钥匙，但快递过程中未锁箱内的东西会丢失。如何安全传递？

三步协议：
1. 你将文件放入箱中，用你的锁锁上 → 寄给同事
2. 同事收到后，用自己的锁再锁一道（现在箱上有两把锁）→ 寄回给你
3. 你收到后，用你的钥匙打开你的锁 → 寄回给同事
4. 同事用自己的钥匙打开，取出文件

💡 这本质上是Diffie-Hellman密钥交换的物理类比——无需共享密钥即可安全通信。

title: 日历骰子
answer:
两个骰子，每面放一个数字（0-9），通过排列两骰子表示01-31的日期。如何放置？

关键洞察：6可以当9用！

必须有的数字：0,0,1,1,2,2（日期11和22需要两个1和两个2，01-09需要两个0）

剩余4个面放3,4,5,6,7,8中的4个 → 但有7个数字！

解决：6和9共用一个面

最终方案：
骰子A：0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
骰子B：0, 1, 2, 6(=9), 7, 8

title: 量化的平均工资
answer:
8个量化分析师想知道团队平均工资，但都不想透露自己的工资。如何实现？

方案：
1. 第一个人选一个随机数R，加上自己的工资S₁，传给第二人
2. 第二人加上S₂，传给第三人
3. ...第八人加上S₈，传回第一个人
4. 第一人减去R，除以8得到平均工资

💡 实际应用：基金持仓数据匿名化——给每个持仓的基金ID加随机数再分发，防止反推策略。

title: 50个智者与玻璃杯
answer:
50个智者被关在各自房间。有一个玻璃杯（初始口朝下）。每分钟苏丹随机叫一人，此人可选择翻转或不翻。当有人正确声明"所有人至少被叫过一次"时全部释放，错误则全部处死。事先可商量策略。

策略：
选1人为"发言人"，其余49人为"计数者"

• 计数者：第一次看到口朝下→翻转为口朝上，之后不再翻
• 发言人：每次看到口朝上→翻为口朝下并计数+1
• 发言人计到49 → 声明所有人被叫过

💡 49人各自翻1次，发言人翻49次收回，计数=49即所有人到过。

title: 七彩帽子（模运算证明）
answer:
7个囚徒，每人戴彩虹七色之一的帽子（颜色可重复），能看到其他6人但看不到自己。各写一个猜测，至少1人猜对则全释放。如何保证？

策略：用模7运算

给颜色编号0-6，设囚徒也编号0-6。
囚徒i的猜测gᵢ满足： (gᵢ + Σ_{k≠i} x_k) mod 7 = i

证明至少1人对：
设真实颜色和为 S = Σ x_k，则 S mod 7 ∈ {0,1,...,6}
当 S mod 7 = i 时，囚徒i猜对（因为gᵢ = i - Σ_{k≠i} x_k mod 7 = x_i mod 7）

S mod 7必等于某个i，所以至少1人猜对。

title: √2是无理数（反证法）
answer:
反证法：假设 √2 = m/n 且 m,n 互质。

m² = 2n² → m²是偶数 → m是偶数
设 m = 2k → 4k² = 2n² → n² = 2k² → n也是偶数

m和n都是偶数 → 有公因子2 → 与互质矛盾！

因此 √2 是无理数。

title: 缺失的整数
answer:
1到100中随机去掉2个数，如何高效找出？

方法（O(n)时间O(1)空间）：

设缺失的数为x和y：
x + y = (1+2+...+100) - Σ(已知数) = 5050 - S₁

x² + y² = (1²+2²+...+100²) - Σ(已知数²) = 338350 - S₂


两个方程两个未知数，解出x和y。
💡 推广：去掉k个数可用前k个幂和方程组，但空间O(k)。

title: 时钟碎成三块
answer:
时钟(1-12)摔成三块，每块数字之和相等。各块上有哪些数字？

Σ(1到12) = 78，每块和 = 26。

注意12和1在钟面上是相邻的！

• 第一块：5, 6, 7, 8 → 和26 ✓
• 第二块：11, 12, 1, 2 → 和26 ✓（12+1=13, 11+2=13）
• 第三块：3, 4, 9, 10 → 和26 ✓

title: 100层楼的鸡蛋
answer:
100层楼，2个鸡蛋。鸡蛋从≥N层扔会碎。最坏情况下最少扔几次确定N？

答案：14次

设最多扔k次，覆盖的楼层数为：
k + (k-1) + (k-2) + ... + 1 = k(k+1)/2 ≥ 100

k=14: 14×15/2 = 105 ≥ 100 ✓
k=13: 13×14/2 = 91 < 100 ✗

策略：14→27→39→50→60→69→77→84→90→95→99→100
碎了则用第2个鸡蛋从上次位置+1逐层试。

title: 25匹马找前3名
answer:
（同前文马赛问题，此处补充说明）

7场比赛：
1-5. 分5组各跑1场（5场）
6. 5个第一名跑第6场
7. 候选马（第6场第1名所在组的2-3名 + 第2名所在组的1-2名 + 第3名所在组的第1名）跑最后一场

💡 核心推理：第6场后可知各组之间的整体快慢关系，排除大量不可能的马。
